data.name: Fadeholm
data.detailed_description:
Endless exploration and adventure awaits those fearless enough to enter. Survival is only the beginning! Fadeholm is a procedural virtual reality (VR) survival dungeon crawler designed in the same vein as old school Nethack and Rogue. As one of the remaining ‘Fade’, the player is challenged to explore the depths of the ancient catacombs in search of an ancient relic. The Fadeholm is as rich as it is dangerous, with room after room filled with riches and items that will make exploration just a little bit easier. The player must manage hunger,health, and endurance while they search every corner of the dungeon, because while the undead hit hard, a Vorpal Warblade of Fire hits harder.

The first chapter, Upper Fadeholm includes:
  • 3 levels of procedural(reproducible random) generated dungeon, expandable to 8 levels through game settings.
  • Multiple unique monsters, each randomized with their own equipment, tactics, and behaviors.
  • Randomized loot throughout the dungeon.
    • Equipment held and worn by monsters is usable upon their defeat.
    • Items become more powerful and enchanted the deeper the player travels
    • Detailed item inspection system aids in determining the power and abilities of the loot discovered.
  • Intuitive movement system:
    • Touchpad movement (4-axis + controller direction control)
    • Armswing locomotion (4 axis + HMD direction control)
    • Teleport for jumping obstacles and quickly manuvering
    • Player can mix and match modes to both controllers.

  • Interactive inventory system:
    • eight active storage locations
    • over the shoulder and hip slots “hot swappable’ allowing quick exchange of items
    • belt slot provides access to various sized satchels for additional storage.
    • independent shield slots on each arm to allow use of items while still employing a shield in combat.
    • wearable headgear
  • Save Game support:
    • Player can save their adventure at anytime and pick up where they left off later.
    • Supports up to three different ‘Engrams’ (save games with history) to enable more than one person adventuring on a single Steam account.
  • Seed (Dimensional Thread) based generation of content:
    • Controls generation of dungeon, monsters, loot, etc.
    • Each Thread generates a unique game play experience.
    • Share a Thread with a friend and compete on the leaderboards, or just see who can explore the furthest!
  • Leader boards, both local and Steam. Rank yourself against your friends and the community. Each board based upon the specific dungeon (dimensional thread) selected.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo: Windows 10
  • Processador: Intel I5-4590, AMD FX8350 or better
  • Memória: 4 MB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GeForce GTX 970, AMD Radeon R9 290 or better
  • DirectX: Versão 11
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 1400 MB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR. Room Scale 2m by 1.5m area required

reviews.review:
edit: The game has not been updated since june, no offer to bugtest playest accepted, nobody is really buying this - this game is dead in the water. avoid.

The game runs very choppy and the controls are unintuitive. items disappear sometimes when dropped, and despite having a gigantic kite shield and intersecting weapon, i cannot block damage. Also, not being able to see the stats on a weapon sort of makes it all seem irrelevent. I may reconsider purchasing this again once the bugs are gone and the game is optimized and the graphics are consistant and all sorts of stuff has been rethought and reworked.

It's not a terrible game, but it's pretty unplayable right now. It's sort of like a less creative version of kings field geared for VR. I love kingsfield, i do not like this game. I'll be following this, but do not puchase this for $20 dollars unless you're willing to take a gamble with a dev to overhaul the game entirely to be more or less comperable to titles such as vanishing realms or vr dungeon knight, which are FAR BETTER in my opinion... I am interested in the depth this game tries to bring, the statistics and such. ALSO, this game needs dropped loot, not just loot chests. A skeleton had a burning mace i would have liked.

edit:

Thank you for responding with some useful information. I'm not entirely against buying this game or playing it again, but the following issues:

-No parrying or cleaving
-Unintuitive controls and inventory
-items disappearing/falling through map
-unoptimized graphics and inconsistent texturing

are all turn offs right now for me. I'd be willing to consider buying this again when these things are fixed, because the premise and the potential is quite good.

I would happily play an evaluation copy and bugtest/critique the game to help out, and would be willing to replace my review with a positive one once things are addressed.
reviews.developer_response:
Thank you for your inputs. We apparently need to emphasise the tutorial more!
 1) Shields must be equipped on your arm, not held in your hand. ‘Held shields’ is a game mechanic that will be available later with cleaving and parry.
 2) Shields are working for both player (when equipped) and monsters.
 3) How to perform item inspection is demonstrated in the tutorial. The inspection system is very detailed providing many data points on every item you can equip. (also see our Guide on 'Fade Lore')
 4) Equipment seen and used by a monster is directly usable once you defeat it. These items just need to be picked up. This includes the magic weapons they use!
 The games controls and interface are different, and can be complex. For the best experience, we recommend players run through the tutorial before attempting to explore!
